South Africa’s Hospitality Sector Faces Acute Credit Squeeze as Bookings Plummet

South Africa’s hospitality industry is facing a severe financial crisis, as a sudden freeze in credit has left many firms struggling to meet payroll and operational costs amid a sharp drop in bookings. The crisis, triggered by a wave of non-performing loans reported by several leading hotel and restaurant groups, has seen banks tighten lending conditions to the sector, locking out even established operators from vital working capital.

Industry insiders report that the effects have been swift and widespread. “In my 30 years in the business, I have never seen a liquidity squeeze of this magnitude,” said Phumzile Ndaba, CEO of the Johannesburg-based hotel chain SunRise Lodges. “We are unable to secure even short-term financing to cover basic expenses, and our advance bookings have fallen by over 60 percent compared to last year.”

According to data released this week by the South African Hospitality Council, occupancy rates at urban hotels have dropped to 32 percent in May, down from 57 percent a year ago. Many operators have responded by shuttering entire floors, reducing hours, or temporarily closing properties. Restaurant owners are reporting similar pressures, with several in Cape Town and Durban announcing indefinite closures.

The sector’s workforce has been especially hard hit. The Hospitality Workers’ Union estimates that over 18,000 jobs have been lost since April, with thousands more staff placed on unpaid leave. “Our members are facing an uncertain future,” said union spokesperson Luyanda Mokoena. “Many have not received salaries for weeks, and retrenchments are accelerating as employers run out of options.”

Analysts warn that without urgent intervention, the crisis could deepen. “The hospitality industry is highly sensitive to both demand shocks and financing constraints,” said Sipho Maduna, a hospitality sector analyst at Kuhle Research. “With credit lines frozen and consumer demand still weak, we expect more firms to default or file for restructuring in the coming weeks.”

Industry bodies are appealing for emergency government support and temporary relief measures to stem further losses. As the crisis continues, operators and workers alike are bracing for continued uncertainty and disruption throughout South Africa’s hospitality sector.
